title: Lifecycle Model — Delivery Lifecycle Specification (ANVIL)
description: Machine-readable authority for the delivery lifecycle model, corpus document 'lifecycle-model' (TS-013-01-02; human-readable counterpart TS-013-01-01). Encodes: the 8-state release state machine with per-edge transition legality (lifecycle-model.md §6.1, §6.4; ADR-003 §4), the activation phase sequence with verify fixed immediately before promote (§5.1; ADR-003 §6.4), rollback target eligibility (R5, §5.2; ADR-003 §7.1, §7.3), installation as an operation creating a Release in Ready rather than a state transition (§6.3; ADR-003 §4), and the machine invariants (R3, R4; ADR-003 §9.1; §6.1 note). Where this schema and lifecycle-model.md disagree, the schema governs (ADR-029 §3).
$comment: Dialect: draft-07, chosen for the widest validator support (python jsonschema, ajv, and mature independent implementations) — maximizing engine-path-independence per ADR-029 §3 and Transition Plan §5.10; no draft-2020-12-only feature is required. Version line (ADR-024 §3.1): the specification carries its own semver line decoupled from runtime releases; the contract major version is the unit of compatibility. This document is corpus version 1.0.0. A breaking change to this model is a governed event requiring an ADR and shipping with a Core major version (ADR-035 §3.1); specification artifacts publish via the spec/ tag line (ADR-024 §3.5). $id is a stable URN — it references the corpus document (lifecycle-model) on its version line and is independent of engine or repository paths; resolvable publication URL mechanics are EPIC-013 scope.

$schema.description: Optional declaration of the schema this lifecycle definition targets (the $id of lifecycle-model.schema.json).

title.description: Optional human-readable title of the lifecycle definition.

description.description: Optional human-readable description of the lifecycle definition.

id.description: Stable identifier of the lifecycle definition.

contractVersion.description: Target contract version of the delivery lifecycle specification (ADR-024 §3.1): semver, decoupled from runtime releases; major version is the compatibility unit.

states.description: The release state machine (lifecycle-model.md §6.1; ADR-003 §4): exactly the 8 contract states; each state declares its legal outgoing transitions per §6.4. There is no 'interrupted' state — recovery is a rule set applied to the last persisted stage (§6.5), not a state.

propertyNames.description: Only the 8 contract states may be declared; invented states (e.g. 'interrupted') are rejected (ADR-003 §4; lifecycle-model.md §6.1 note).

transitions.description: Legal targets from Ready (§6.4): activation requested, set aside without activation, or deleted before activation. The edge set is fixed — omitting a legal edge is non-conforming (ADR-003 §4).

Legal targets from Activating (§6.4): promotion commits, activation failed with rollback, or activation failed without rollback. The edge set is fixed — omitting a legal edge is non-conforming (ADR-003 §4).

Legal targets from Active (§6.4): rollback requested, or archived (automatic when a new Release is activated; explicit when retired). The edge set is fixed — omitting a legal edge is non-conforming (ADR-003 §4).
Legal targets from Rolling Back (§6.4): rollback completed as a forward transition, or rollback failed. The edge set is fixed — omitting a legal edge is non-conforming (ADR-003 §4).
Legal targets from Rolled Back (§6.4): preserved for reference, or deleted. The edge set is fixed — omitting a legal edge is non-conforming (ADR-003 §4).

Legal targets from Archived (§6.4): rollback restore — the forward transition rollback executes on the target (R5; ADR-003 §7.1, §7.3) — or explicit cleanup. The edge set is fixed — omitting a legal edge is non-conforming (ADR-003 §4).

Legal targets from Failed (§6.4): retry activation after verification passed (recoverable), retired after failure, or deleted after failure. The edge set is fixed — omitting a legal edge is non-conforming (ADR-003 §4).
Removed is the terminal state (§6.4; ADR-003 §4.10): no further transitions — the transition list must be empty.

activation.description: The activation phase sequence (lifecycle-model.md §5.1; ADR-003 §6.4): prepare → configure → framework phases (0..n declared) → verify (immediately before promote, may be empty) → promote. The phase sequence is defined by the Specification; phase content is declared by the standard.

phaseSequence.description: Comma-separated declaration of the full phase sequence in execution order. Fixed positions: 'prepare' first, 'configure' second, 'verify' immediately before 'promote', 'promote' last (the atomic commitment point). Between configure and verify, 0..n declared framework phases may appear. Framework phase names must not collide with reserved phase names (case-insensitive); a sequence that omits promote, reorders prepare/configure, or places verify after promote is rejected.

verify.description: Declared verify content. Verify occupies the fixed position immediately before promote; a standard may declare zero checks, in which case the phase is a no-op gate (§5.1).

rollback.description: Rollback is a first-class lifecycle operation, not a reverse activation (§5.2; ADR-003 §7): it restores the previously active Release by a forward transition and preserves the rolled-back Release for inspection. Legality is defined by state (R5).

targetSelection.description: R5 / §5.2 operational definition: the rollback target is the Archived Release with the newest archival timestamp among Releases that were previously Active.

targetState.description: R5 / §5.2: the rollback target must be in state Archived — the state every superseded Active Release enters when a new Release is activated. Any other target state is rejected.

installation.description: Installation is an operation, not a state-machine transition (§6.3; ADR-003 §4): it creates a Release directly in Ready from a verified Artifact; it does not move an existing Release. Activation targets the resulting Release, never an uploaded Artifact.

operation.description: The only lifecycle operation that creates a Release (§6.3).

createsState.description: Installation creates the Release in state Ready (§6.3; ADR-003 §4).

isStateTransition.description: Installation creates a Release, it does not transition one (§6.3).

invariants.description: Machine invariants declared by a conforming lifecycle definition. These invariants hold at all times (ADR-003 §9) and are encoded here as documented constraints because they span Releases and cannot be checked on a single definition document.

oneActiveRelease.description: R3 / ADR-003 §9.1: at any time, at most one Release is in the Active state; when a new Release is activated, the previously active Release automatically becomes Archived.

activationIsAtomic.description: R4 / §5.1: activation is atomic from the observer's perspective — either the new Release serves, or the previous one still does; nothing after the commitment point is assumed.

interruptedIsNotAState.description: §6.1 note, §6.5: there is no 'interrupted' state in the machine; interruptions are recorded and reconciled explicitly by the recovery rules.

stateEntry.description: A state entry: the list of legal outgoing transitions.

transitions.description: Legal outgoing transitions from this state (lifecycle-model.md §6.4).
